stations.title: Chest Pain — STEMI
stations.task: Evaluate a patient with acute chest pain and manage ST-elevation MI

patient.name: John Miller
patient.opening: Doctor, I have this crushing pain in my chest that started about an hour ago.

keySymptoms: Acute central chest pain radiating to left arm

mustAsk: What does the pain feel like?
bonus: Ask about family history of heart disease

questions.question: What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.answer: Activate STEMI protocol and obtain stat ECG

stations.title: Acute Dyspnea — Pulmonary Embolism
stations.task: Assess a patient with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain after a long-haul flight

patient.name: Sarah Johnson
patient.opening: I suddenly feel very short of breath and my chest hurts when I breathe in.

bonus: Ask about leg pain or swelling

questions.question: What is the next imaging study?

stations.title: Stroke Assessment
stations.task: Evaluate a patient with acute stroke symptoms for thrombolysis eligibility

patient.name: Robert Davis
patient.opening: (Unable to speak clearly — facial droop on right side)

mustAsk: When was the patient last seen normal?

questions.question: What is the time window for tPA?
questions.answer: Within 3 hours (extended to 4.5 hours for eligible patients)

stations.title: Acute Asthma Exacerbation
stations.task: Manage a patient with severe acute asthma exacerbation

patient.name: Emily Chen
patient.opening: (Wheezing audibly, speaking in short phrases) I can't breathe...

questions.question: What is the first treatment?
questions.answer: High-flow oxygen and continuous nebulized salbutamol with ipratropium

stations.title: Upper GI Bleed — Variceal Hemorrhage
stations.task: Manage a patient with acute variceal hemorrhage

hiddenProfile.diagnosis: Esophageal variceal hemorrhage due to portal hypertension from alcoholic liver disease
pastHistory: Alcohol use disorder (1 L whiskey daily for 10 years)

mustAsk: How much blood have you vomited?
bonus: Ask about alcohol use and family history

questions.question: What medication should be administered for suspected variceal bleeding?

stations.title: ACE Inhibitor-Induced Angioedema
stations.task: Manage a patient with ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema and airway compromise

patient.name: Maria Garcia
patient.opening: (Swollen lips and tongue, speaking with difficulty) My face is swelling up...

mustAsk: Have you started any new medications?
bonus: Ask about prior episodes of angioedema

questions.question: What is the first priority?
questions.answer: Airway assessment and prepare for difficult intubation
